original_question: Let phi(k, G) denote the number of k-matchings in a graph G. For integers q >= 1, r >= 1, and 1 <= k <= qr, is the maximum number of k-matchings among all simple r-regular graphs on 2qr vertices attained by the disjoint union of q copies of the complete bipartite graph K_{r,r}? Equivalently, does Theta(k, qr, r) = phi(k, qK_{r,r}) hold for every k = 1, ..., qr, where Theta(k, n, r) is the maximum of phi(k, G) over simple r-regular graphs G on 2n vertices?
target_in_paper: Section 1 (Introduction), equation (1.7): the Upper Matching Conjecture (UMC). This draft does not target Conjecture 1.1 of the survey, which is a different non-bipartite lower-bound question.
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s intended statement almost exactly: it uses the correct counting function φ(k,G), the correct extremal quantity Θ(k,n,r), the correct host class of simple r-regular graphs on 2qr vertices, the correct candidate extremal graph qK_{r,r}, and the correct quantifier range k=1,...,qr. This is essentially the UMC as stated in Section 1, equation (1.7).
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone in the paper’s notation, explicitly define Θ(k,n,r):=max{φ(k,G): G∈𝒢(2n,r)}, where 𝒢(2n,r) is the set of simple r-regular graphs on 2n vertices.
State that qG denotes the disjoint union of q copies of a graph G; this is the paper’s notation used in the sentence immediately before (1.7).
For maximum paper-faithfulness, identify the statement by name as the Upper Matching Conjecture (UMC).
Disambiguate it from Conjecture 1.1 of the same survey, which concerns exponential growth of ω(n,n,r) for fixed r≥3 and is not the same problem.
refined_question: Upper Matching Conjecture (UMC). Let 𝒢(2n,r) denote the set of simple r-regular graphs on 2n vertices, let φ(k,G) be the number of k-matchings of G, and define Θ(k,n,r):=max{φ(k,G): G∈𝒢(2n,r)}. If qG denotes the disjoint union of q copies of G, then for every pair of positive integers q and r, and every k=1,...,qr, is it true that Θ(k,qr,r)=φ(k,qK_{r,r})?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for every q,r≥1 and every k∈{1,...,qr}, does the disjoint union qK_{r,r} maximize the number of k-matchings among all simple r-regular graphs on 2qr vertices?
justification: The nearest official formulation in the paper is not the survey’s numbered Conjecture 1.1, but the Upper Matching Conjecture stated in Section 1 as equation (1.7), after the definitions of 𝒢(2n,r), Θ(k,n,r), and qG in (1.1) and the surrounding introductory notation. The sentence before (1.7) also gives the perfect-matching case Θ(qr,qr,r)=φ(qr,qK_{r,r})=(r!)^q as motivation. Your draft already reproduces the mathematical content of (1.7) with only minor notational/contextual details missing. This is a purely finite graph-theoretic statement, so ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, and nilpotency conditions are not applicable here.
